description: Search file contents with a regular expression (Python re syntax), like grep -rn. Default output: one line per match, PATH:LINE:TEXT; paste PATH into read and use LINE as its offset. "files": true lists only the matching files. "glob" limits which files are searched (e.g. "*.py", "src/**/*.json"); "fixed": true searches for the plain text; "context": N adds N lines around each match. Skips binary files, files over 8MB, names starting with . (unless "hidden": true) and, inside a git work tree, files ignored by .gitignore (unless "gitignore": false). At most max_matches per call; a last line "... next_offset N" means more: call again with offset N. To find files by name, use glob. Errors: PatternBad (fix the regular expression, or use "fixed": true), FileMissing.

pattern.description: the regular expression (Python re), matched against one line at a time

path.description: a folder (searched with everything under it) or one file, relative to your workspace or absolute (default .)

glob.description: only search files whose path under path matches this (e.g. *.py, src/**/*.json)

fixed.description: true = pattern is plain text, not a regular expression

ignore_case.description: true = upper and lower case are the same

context.description: lines to show before and after each match (0 to 5)

files.description: true = only list matching files, one per line: PATH TAB number of matching lines

hidden.description: true = also search names starting with .

gitignore.description: false = also search files that .gitignore ignores

offset.description: first match to show (default 0; with files, first file)

max_matches.description: most matches to show (default 100, at most 500; with files, most files)
